narrative: Demand for PL3__M5BF99BE is intermittent (CV=0.667) with 92.5% non-zero working days and a statistically significant downward trend (t=-4.11). Lead times are short but highly unstable (CV=0.786), making safety stock the critical buffer. An (r,Q) continuous-review model is recommended with Q=1,448 units (EOQ capped at storage limit) and safety stock of 423 units, delivering a 68% annual cost reduction versus the current zero-buffer SAP policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With 92.5% non-zero demand days and a moderate CV of 0.667, demand is sufficiently regular for a continuous-review trigger. Short but volatile lead times (mean=1.18d, CV=0.786) make continuous monitoring preferable over periodic review to avoid stockouts from sudden lead-time spikes. Fixed Q simplifies procurement scheduling and leverages the EOQ cost structure.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage constraint is binding: EOQ of 2,121 was capped to 1,448 units. This increases ordering frequency slightly (~38 vs 26 orders/year at unconstrained EOQ) and raises annual ordering costs by ~$900, but remains well below the current SAP cost. If storage can be expanded by ~250 units, the full EOQ would become feasible.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ(271) + SS(423) = 694 is below max_storage_units(1871.645); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
